speech_verification.heard: A grizzly bear left Hugh Glass for dead in a shallow grave. In 1823, the bear mauled Glass and punctured his throat. Two companions abandoned him, stealing his rifle and his supplies. Glass survived by eating insects and letting maggots clean his wounds. When he finally caught the men, he chose mercy over revenge. He forgave the men who left him in a shallow grave.

notes.hook: Excellent, gripping hook that immediately sets up a legendary survival story.
notes.clarity: Saying a grizzly bear left him in a shallow grave is confusing and historically inaccurate.
notes.payoff: The twist of choosing forgiveness over expected bloody revenge is highly satisfying.
notes.visuals: Features an anachronistic map in beat 2 and geographically incorrect California scenery in beat 4.
notes.loop: The loop is grammatically clunky and repeats the grave reference awkwardly.

frames.problem: The reservation map is anachronistic for 1823 and illegible at phone size.
The landscape photo shows Mendocino, California, which is geographically incorrect for South Dakota.

rewrite: Beat 1: Change to 'After a grizzly attack, Hugh Glass was abandoned in a shallow grave.'
Beat 2: Change to 'In 1823, the beast mauled him so badly his throat was punctured.'
Beat 6: Change to 'Yet when he finally tracked them down, he forgave the men.'
rounds.better_than_last: This Short does a better job of incorporating an actual archival portrait of one of the real historical participants (Jim Bridger) in beat 5.
